summary: Iteration 12 – Members module (team management with roles & permissions) backend tests. Created /app/backend/tests/test_members.py with 15 tests covering full CRUD, sort order, default values, 404 handling, multi-user isolation (user A vs user B), and auth guards. All 15 new tests PASS. Full regression suite (163 tests, including the 148 pre-existing) also PASSES. No issues found.

minor.issue: Idempotent: deleting an unknown id returns 200 {ok:true} instead of 404. Consistent with existing /api/staff and /api/owners behavior, so probably intentional. Documented in test_delete_unknown_is_idempotent.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1679 – update_member returns db.members.find_one({'id': member_id}, ...) without user_id filter. Since the update_one above already filters on user_id, the doc necessarily belongs to the caller, so it's safe. Could still be tightened for defense-in-depth (add user_id to the find_one filter) to be consistent with get_member.

server.py:1684 – delete_member always returns {ok:true} even when nothing was deleted. Consistent with /api/staff, /api/owners pattern; acceptable but note that clients cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'deleted'.

MemberIn model has no validation on `email` (no EmailStr) nor on `role`/`language` (no Enum). Free-form strings are accepted. Consider Pydantic EmailStr and Literal[...] for role/language if business rules require it.
server.py file size is 2106 lines – exceeds the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting per-domain routers (members.py, owners.py, staff.py, ...).
seed_data_creation: Two isolated test users (user_TEST_A_* and user_TEST_B_*) with matching entries in Mongo `users` and `user_sessions` collections. All test members are prefixed TEST_ and cleaned up in fixture teardown (db.members.delete_many + user_sessions + users).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable Members test file at /app/backend/tests/test_members.py. Uses two module-scoped users (A/B) built directly in Mongo to bypass Google OAuth (following the pattern from conftest.py). Auth endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <session_token>. BASE_URL is resolved from backend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL, falling back to frontend/.env.
